title: Global Food-Price Forecastability Atlas v1 - does market-local weather add predictive value?
question: Across the countries for which WFP publishes enough monthly retail food prices, do market-local rainfall and temperature anomalies improve out-of-sample forecasts of staple-food price changes beyond a model that uses price history alone?
hypothesis: Adding market-local weather anomalies (family B) to price history (family A) lowers the country-balanced mean squared error of 1-month (H1) and 3-month (H2) log price-change forecasts over the common evaluation window.
estimand: Ratio of country-balanced mean squared forecast errors, ridge family B over ridge family A, on matched forecasts (same series, origin and target) with forecast origins from 2022-01, at horizons of 1 and 3 months. Each country present in an origin month has equal weight.

spec.title: Global Food-Price Forecastability Atlas v1 - does market-local weather add predictive value?
spec.question: Across the countries for which WFP publishes enough monthly retail food prices, do market-local rainfall and temperature anomalies improve out-of-sample forecasts of staple-food price changes beyond a model that uses price history alone?
spec.hypothesis: Adding market-local weather anomalies (family B) to price history (family A) lowers the country-balanced mean squared error of 1-month (H1) and 3-month (H2) log price-change forecasts over the common evaluation window.
spec.estimand: Ratio of country-balanced mean squared forecast errors, ridge family B over ridge family A, on matched forecasts (same series, origin and target) with forecast origins from 2022-01, at horizons of 1 and 3 months. Each country present in an origin month has equal weight.

population.selection_rule: per country, the commodity groups with the most eligible series (ties by commodity code); eligibility is computed from metadata only (counts, coverage, gaps), never from model performance

timing.vintage_statement: Backtests use today's revised data; original publication dates are not available from the providers, so information timing is an explicitly assumed release lag, not an observed real-time vintage.

hypotheses.statement: Family B (price history + market-local weather) has lower 1-month forecast loss than family A.
Family B (price history + market-local weather) has lower 3-month forecast loss than family A.

inference.unit_of_inference: forecast-origin month: losses are averaged within each month before testing, so thousands of market-month forecasts are not treated as independent observations

limitations: Market-local weather is NASA POWER reanalysis at the market's grid cell, a geographic proxy; it is not the weather where the traded crop was grown.
Prices are nominal local-currency WFP retail prices; no deflation or currency conversion.
Predictive, not causal. An improvement would show that weather information helps forecasts, not that weather causes price changes.

The evaluation window (2022-2026) includes global commodity and currency shocks shared by many countries; the two-way bootstrap and month-level test account for shared shocks but cannot make a short window long.
CHIRPS was not integrated, so no alternative precipitation source is compared in v1.

families.A: price history only (lags, momentum, volatility, seasonality)
families.B: A + market-local weather anomalies (NASA POWER at the market's grid cell)

headline: 113 commodity groups in 39 countries. H1 (h=1): no improvement established (-1.9% loss); H2 (h=3): no improvement established (+0.5% loss).

freeze.statement: Groups were selected from observation metadata (counts, coverage, gaps, coordinates) without estimating any model on this population.
